test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 8 Oct 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A solid metallic cylinder with a base radius of 3 cm and a height 120 of cm is melted and recast into a sphere of radius r cm. What is the value of r if there is a 10% metal loss in the conversion?
solution:
Given:

Base radius of the cylinder = 3 cm 

Height of the cylinder = 120 cm.

Concept used:

The volume of a cylinder = π × R2 × H unit³ (R & H being the radius and the height of the cylinder respectively)

The volume of a sphere = 4/3 × π × r3 (r being the radius of the sphere)

Calculation:

Volume of the metallic cylinder = π × 3² × 120 = 1080π cm³

Effective metallic volume = 1080π - 1080π × 10% = 972π cm3

According to the question,

4/3 × π × r³ = 972π

⇒ r3 = 729

⇒ r = 9

**∴ The radius of the recast sphere is 9 cm.**
